title: Bold Ignored (Print Only)

illustrates.quote: Ignore font attributes when they are used as a simple visual enhancement for print layout, e.g., a heavier font used for instructions, italics used for a dedication, etc.

blocks.text: **For additional reading, go to InfoTrac College Edition, your online research library at http://web1.infotrac-college.com**
blocks.features: Bold instructional banner (a heavier font used for instructions, per rule 5.3.6's own example wording) beside a small decorative icon.

blocks.text: Enter the search terms ... using Key Terms. (four lines)
blocks.features: Four plain-weight instruction lines; the proper-name search terms embedded in each are italicized.

print.notes: Explicitly '(Print Only)' — the source gives no braille rendering for this example; the point of the example is the ignored bold banner, so no transcription is expected.
print.surroundingText: Follows rule 5.3.6 directly; Example 5-6 (also Print Only) immediately follows on the same printed page (5-5).
print.printFeatures: Boxed callout with a small icon, bold instructional banner, and four plain instruction lines each containing one italicized proper name.

braille.notes: Print Only — the source shows no braille transcription for this example, only the caption 'Example 5-5: Bold Ignored (Print Only)' and the print picture; none is guessed.

resolution: Both runs agree this is Print Only with no braille; print content synthesized from both runs' PDF reads (p.131, printed page 5-5), which agree on substance.
